paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the God of heaven knows what no one else can know, and He rules over everything, even kings. The wise men said, "No one on earth can do what the king requests!" (Daniel 2:10). They were right about the earth. But Daniel says, "there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries" (Daniel 2:28). When you hit a wall that nobody on earth can get you over, that's not the end of the road, baker.

Look at how Daniel handles it. He doesn't panic, and he doesn't take the credit. He asks his friends to plead for mercy from the God of heaven (Daniel 2:18), and when the answer comes, he says it came "not because I have more wisdom than any man alive" (Daniel 2:30). He blessed God first and walked to the king second. I once thought my whole story ended in the back of a junk drawer, and I'm telling you, praying with friends beats panicking by yourself EVERY time.

And then the statue. Gold, silver, bronze, iron, clay, and every one of those kingdoms gets shattered, but the kingdom the God of heaven sets up "will never be destroyed" and "will itself stand forever" (Daniel 2:44). Daniel says "He changes the times and seasons; He removes kings and establishes them" (Daniel 2:21). So the powers that look so big today are not the ones holding history. God is, and that's why you can rest, baker, even when the headlines look like iron mixed with clay.
